summary: Inspect a trusted pre-extracted sequence of model checkpoints through comparable metrics and one fixed declared projection without loading or executing checkpoint binaries.
objective: Inspect a trusted pre-extracted sequence of model checkpoints through comparable metrics and one fixed declared projection without loading or executing checkpoint binaries.
intent_signals: Inspect supplied training checkpoints along one fixed projected trajectory.
Compare checkpoint metrics without pretending the 3D path is full parameter-space distance.
example_prompts: Inspect supplied training checkpoints along one fixed projected trajectory.
negative_signals: Loading arbitrary pickle or executing an untrusted model.
not_for: Loading arbitrary pickle or executing an untrusted model.
Inferring why training changed from a projected path or loss trace.

entities.name: Checkpoint ledger
entities.guidance: Store stable checkpoint ID, run ID, step/epoch, hashes, framework/version and available component names.

entities.name: Fixed projection frame
entities.guidance: Use one supplied center c and one 3×D basis B for all checkpoints; axes and basis hash stay visible.

entities.name: Metric rails
entities.guidance: Separate training metrics from fixed-evaluation metrics and retain dataset/split/evaluator provenance.

state_contract.model: Accept 2..64 trusted, pre-extracted manifest entries from one declared run. Each entry has unique ID, integer step, optional epoch, component hashes, metric records with split/evaluator IDs, and optionally a finite parameter vector theta_t of a shared declared key/shape/order with D in [1,4096]. For spatial display require one finite fixed B in R^(3×D) and center c in R^D, supplied or derived once from the complete accepted set and then frozen; y_t=B(theta_t-c). Do not deserialize or execute `.pt`, `.pth`, pickle, TorchScript or arbitrary code. If vectors are absent, accept supplied projection coordinates only when their method, center, basis/hash and source checkpoint IDs are present, and disable full-space distance checks.
state_contract.authority: Supplied finite tensors, ordered identifiers, basis conventions and provenance own semantic state. Blender/glTF assets are display-only; Three.js owns validation, calculation, linked selection, failure states and exact reset.
actions: Select/step checkpoints in source step order.
Compare named metrics only when split/evaluator definitions match.
Toggle projected path, metric rails and full-space distance when available.
Reset checkpoint, projection and metric selections.

invariants: Every displayed point uses the same center, basis, parameter key order and D.
A 3D segment length is labeled projected distance; full parameter-space distance is shown only from compatible complete vectors.
Metrics with different dataset, split, preprocessing or evaluator identity are not placed on one comparable scale without an explicit bridge.
Untrusted or executable checkpoint containers remain unavailable rather than being opened.
motion_guidance: Playback follows discrete checkpoint steps; interpolation is a display bridge and never an unsaved training state.
creative_affordances: Choose any coherent laboratory, constellation or sculptural art direction while preserving exact labels, selectable identity and non-color encodings.
known_limits: Documentary authored recipe only; no model training, checkpoint execution, quantum hardware, Blender export, browser, renderer or interactive runtime was run.
glTF transports neutral display assets only; tensors, checkpoints, citations, basis order, dtype and provenance remain external data.
The optional evaluation view displays supplied scalar metrics only; it does not run probes or infer generalization.

claims.statement: PyTorch documents a general training checkpoint as a dictionary that may include epoch, model state_dict, optimizer state_dict and loss, and explains that optimizer state is needed to resume training state.
claims.scope: PyTorch checkpoint organization example; it does not define cross-run comparability or a universal checkpoint schema.

source_refs.locator: What is a state_dict?; Saving & Loading a General Checkpoint, save/load examples and explanatory paragraphs

claims.statement: PyTorch security guidance says models are programs, warns that running untrusted models is equivalent to running untrusted code, and advises treating checkpoint trust and deserialization as a security boundary.
claims.scope: PyTorch security guidance current when read; the recipe avoids deserialization entirely and does not certify any format as universally safe.

source_refs.locator: Using PyTorch Securely; Untrusted models; distributed checkpoint trust warning

object_craft.structure: Blender authors neutral checkpoint pylons, metric rails and a reusable three-axis projection cage; no weights or training data enter glTF.
object_craft.material: Glyph shape separates saved state, metric observation and unavailable comparison; line style marks projection versus full-space readout.
object_craft.articulation: Three.js ingests validated pre-extracted JSON, owns step ordering, projection arithmetic, comparability gates, provenance panels and exact reset.

physical_contract.scope: Finite imported-data calculation and explanatory playback; no physical dynamics, model training, quantum device or causal attribution.
state: declared dimensions, basis and numeric tolerance
checks: Every displayed point uses the same center, basis, parameter key order and D.
A 3D segment length is labeled projected distance; full parameter-space distance is shown only from compatible complete vectors.
Metrics with different dataset, split, preprocessing or evaluator identity are not placed on one comparable scale without an explicit bridge.
